business.title: High-κ bismuth molybdate single-crystalline dielectric for high-temperature two-dimensional transistors
business.description: Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors represent promising alternatives to traditional silicon for next-generation electronic devices. However, there are still significant challenges in high-temperature 2D electronic devices integrated by existing high-κ dielectrics. Here, we report a BiOCl-assisted chemical vapor deposition method to synthesize high-quality bismuth molybdate (Bi2MoO6) single-crystalline nanosheets with controllable thickness and good thermal stability. High-κ (54.2) nature is identified within as-grown Bi2MoO6 nanosheets, with wide bandgap (∼3.85 eV) and large breakdown field strength (∼3.9 MV/cm) at room temperature. As results, Bi2MoO6 top-gate MoS2 transistor exhibits a negligible hysteresis and an average subthreshold swing less than 100 mV dec−1 within 3 orders of magnitude of current range, as well as excellent operational stability. Moreover, the transistor maintains a high on/off current ratio of > 104 and a hysteresis of less than 10 mV/(MV cm−1) at the high temperature up to 500 K, meeting the requirements of high-temperature electronic devices. The inverter with Bi2MoO6 gate dielectric is also achieved, yielding a high gain of 86.1 at supply voltage of 5 V. This work enriches the high-κ gate dielectric family and provides considerable application potential in high-temperature electronic devices. High temperature stability is an important requirement for future electronic circuits based on 2D semiconductors. Here, the authors report the synthesis of high-κ (54.2) Bi2MoO6 single-crystalline nanosheets and their application as gate dielectric for 2D MoS2 transistors, showing good thermal stability of the devices up to 500 K.

science.title: Reliability improvement of distribution networks through optimal recloser placement considering photovoltaic resource allocation and sizing with protection coordination constraints
science.description: This study presents an integrated optimization framework for the optimal placement of reclosers and the simultaneous determination of the location and capacity of photovoltaic (PV) units in distribution networks. Unlike conventional approaches that treat the placement of protection devices and PV allocation as separate planning problems, the proposed method addresses both problems simultaneously and evaluates the impact of PV integration on protection performance and network reliability. Within this framework, recloser placement aims to improve reliability indices, including SAIFI, SAIDI, and ENS, while the locations of PV units and the maximum hosting capacity are determined subject to network voltage constraints. In addition, the coordination constraint between the recloser and cut-out fuse is incorporated into the objective function as a penalty term to ensure proper protection coordination and maintain the fuse-saving strategy. The optimization problem is solved using a search algorithm, and the proposed method is evaluated on the IEEE 33-bus test system. In Scenario 2, Bus 29 is identified as the optimal location for a PV unit with a capacity equivalent to 70% of the total network load, resulting in an improved voltage profile. In Scenario 3, with the recloser optimally placed on Line 1, the ENS, SAIFI, and SAIDI values are 36.82 (MWh/yr), 5.58 (int/cus/yr) and 9.12 (h/cus/yr), respectively. Furthermore, the short-circuit analysis of faults downstream of the cut-out fuses confirms that the recloser–fuse coordination constraint is satisfied both with and without PV integration. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework can simultaneously optimize recloser placement and PV allocation while maintaining proper protection coordination and the fuse-saving strategy. It also enables an increase in PV hosting capacity subject to voltage constraints and improves network reliability.

science.title: Evaluating explanation methods by the predictors they induce
science.description: Explanations of machine learning models are usually judged by criteria that are hard to compare. We propose a simpler test: if an explanation really describes how a model uses its features, it should be possible to rebuild the model’s predictions from it. We turn each explanation into a predictor by reading each feature’s effect and adding them up, and measure how well that predictor reproduces the model on unseen data. Nothing is fitted, so the score reflects the explanation itself. The test applies to any explanation that can be written as a function of the features; we demonstrate it on partial dependence plots (PDP), accumulated local effects (ALE), SHAP and LIME. We prove that summing partial dependence curves gives the best possible additive summary of a model when its features are independent, and that this fails when they are dependent. Across 13 real datasets and 9 synthetic designs and four model families, which method scores best depends entirely on feature dependence: where features are independent SHAP is slightly worse than PDP, exactly as the theory predicts; on dependent real data SHAP leads. Some widely used quality metrics can even prefer a randomly permuted explanation to an intact one.

science.title: Optical observation of ultrafast carrier separation in InGaN photocatalyst nanostructures
science.description: Understanding carrier dynamics in semiconductor nanostructures is essential for optimizing their photocatalytic performance. We present direct optical evidence of ultrafast carrier separation in InGaN nanostructures used for water splitting. Two types of InGaN-based photocatalysts are studied: deepnano structures, which are a p-type InGaN micro-network, and nanowires incorporating an InGaN/GaN layered heterostructure. Here, we show that rapid lateral carrier separation in these nanostructures produces observable signatures in ultrafast spectroscopy. Using combined time-resolved photoluminescence and time-resolved differential reflectance spectroscopy, we observe photoluminescence exhibiting fast decay while differential reflection remains stable. This indicates rapid carrier separation. Studies of temperature and power-dependent photoluminescence confirm that carrier separation dominates over recombination-driven decay, and Mg doping studies reveal that stronger band bending enhances the carrier separation. The physical interpretation of the observations is supported by a numerical model including drift, diffusion, and thermal relaxation. The results provide critical insights into charge carrier dynamics in InGaN nanostructures, highlighting their potential for efficient photocatalysis. The authors show that ultrafast carrier separation causes the rapid photoluminescence decay in nanostructured InGaN photocatalysts from time resolved photoluminescence and differential reflectance spectroscopy supported by numerical modelling.
